title: Ordinary counit comparison transport between derived tensor models
statement: Let $R,A,B,D$ be commutative rings, let $A,B$ be $R$-algebras, put $E=A\otimes_R B$, and let $D$ be an $E$-algebra [def-weil-module-base-change]. Choose derived categories of $R$- and $B$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $s:P\to G$ be a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of $A$-modules, and choose models $M_P,M_G$ of their base-derived tensor cohomology [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model]. For every $i\in\mathbf Z$ there is an $E$-linear isomorphism $e:T_{P,i}\simeq T_{G,i}$ such that $\beta_{P,i}\gg H^i(E\otimes_A s)=e\gg\beta_{G,i}$. The maps $\beta$ are the ordinary comparison fields of the models; no ordinary tensor map is assumed invertible.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change, independence of choices; perfect.tex equation-bc before Tag 0DJ8, canonical comparison

proof.text: Restrict s to R. Mathlib exact restriction of scalars preserves homology, so DerivedCategory.Qh sends its homotopy class to an isomorphism. Install the universal fields of both models. Functor.leftDerivedUnique gives their counit-compatible natural isomorphism eta. Whisker eta with B-cohomology and compose the image of s, the two cohomologyIso maps and this natural isomorphism, giving a B-linear isomorphism eb.

Naturality of eta and (a id_P) composed with s = s composed with (a id_G), followed by cohomologyIso_smul, give U.map((a tensor 1) id) composed with eb.hom = eb.hom composed with U.map((a tensor 1) id). On elements this says eb is compatible with a tensor 1. Its B-linearity handles 1 tensor b. Tensor induction extends compatibility to all scalars of E, using a tensor b = (a tensor 1)(1 tensor b), zero and addition. Bundle e0 as an E-linear map. Its underlying function equals eb.hom and is bijective, so ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective gives the E-linear isomorphism e.

The ordinaryIso generator equation proves naturality under s degree by degree: test on 1 tensor q using ExtendScalars.hom_ext, then both composites are (1 tensor 1) tensor s(q). Apply homology. The equation leftDerivedNatTrans_app pins eta to the universal counits. Combine this equation with eta naturality and counit naturality for s, and apply B-cohomology. Naturality of homologyFunctorFactorsh, homologyFunctorFactors and the restriction homology isomorphism joins this square to the ordinaryIso square. Apply faithful restriction of scalars to the desired equality, replace the restriction of e by eb, cancel the restriction homology isomorphism, and substitute comparison_eq. The preceding naturality identities, composed and reassociated, give exactly the comparison square.
